title: Reflected XSS in User Rendered Content
description: Instances of unescaped user-generated content were found in `innerHTML` assignments resulting in potential XSS vulnerabilities.
impact: An attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the context of the user's session, which could lead to data theft, credential compromise, or malware distribution.
technical_analysis: The application returns user-generated content directly without proper sanitization, allowing the execution of attacker-controlled scripts when inserted into the DOM through unsafe methods like `innerHTML`.
poc_description:
1. Navigate to the affected page (e.g., public-profile.html).
2. Inject the payload: `<script>alert(1)</script>` in user input fields.
3. Observe that the alert is executed, confirming a successful XSS vulnerability.
remediation_steps: Implement proper output encoding and sanitization for all user-generated content. Utilize libraries like DOMPurify to prevent script injections. Ensure proper Content Security Policy (CSP) is enforced to mitigate XSS attempts.
evidence: When injecting `<script>alert(1)</script>`, an alert box appears, indicating successful execution of the injected script.
assumptions: Assumes that the attacker can exploit the input without any constraints on the input length or character set.
